chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Abdullah ibn Ubay ibn Salul died, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was present at his funeral. Umar said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'O Messenger of Allah! Has not Allah forbidden you from standing at his grave?' So he was silent. Umar said again, 'O Messenger of Allah! Has not Allah forbidden you from standing at his grave?' So he said to him, 'Woe be unto you! And what do you know what I said? I said: O Allah! Fill his belly with fire, and fill his grave with fire, and his origin with fire.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Thus he exposed from the Messenger of Allah what he disliked (to expose).'

key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُبَيِّ: Abdullah ibn Ubay, leader of the hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Medina

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet (SAWW) remain silent when Umar questioned him about praying for Abdullah ibn Ubay?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the Prophet's (SAW) outward silence and his inward invocation of specific punishment for Abdullah ibn Ubay, the leader of the hypocrites (Munafiqun). It illustrates the Shia scholarly understanding that the Prophet's presence at the funeral was not a general intercession for forgiveness, but a deliberate act of declaring divine retribution, thereby clarifying the nuance of the Quranic verse 9:84. The incident underscores the concept of 'Ibda' (manifestation), where the Prophet reveals a hidden meaning to Umar that was not immediately apparent.
